rpo.note: RPO is now nearly 10x FY revenue, giving the bull case huge contractual visibility.

rpoconv.note: Revenue conversion remains tiny versus backlog, keeping the delivery bear case alive.

oci.note: OCI growth accelerated again and is the clearest operating validation of demand.

airunrate.note: Annualized OCI revenue is scaling fast, though still small versus RPO.

capex.note: FY capex intensity is extreme, front-loading risk before backlog conversion.

fcf.note: Negative FCF margin is the sharpest crack in the AI buildout thesis.

debt.note: FY debt financing was massive and raises balance-sheet sensitivity to execution delays.

power.note: Secured power capacity helps de-risk physical delivery of the cloud backlog.

rs.note: Today’s relative underperformance shows the tape is pushing back on financing risk.

iv.note: Elevated options premium shows traders are pricing a large execution-risk move.

insider.note: Recent open-market insider selling appears modest versus historical Oracle sales.

rev.note: Consensus EPS has edged up, but revisions are not yet matching the RPO narrative.

ORCL.summary: Oracle’s AI backlog is extraordinary, but the verified conversion, capex, FCF and financing load make execution risk the swing factor.

azure.note: Azure accelerated sharply and remains the number the bull case needs.

airunrate.note: AI ARR has scaled materially, validating Microsoft’s monetization lead.

capex.note: Quarterly PPE additions are rising faster than revenue, keeping ROIC concerns live.

fcf.note: FCF remains large but is compressing as AI infrastructure spend absorbs cash.

gm.note: Microsoft Cloud margin fell as AI depreciation and usage costs increased.

power.note: Contracted renewable supply supports multi-year data-center scaling.

rs.note: The stock lagged tech materially today, showing capex worries are weighing.

iv.note: Options imply moderate event risk, not a panic hedge setup.

insider.note: Recent insider sales are small relative to Microsoft’s scale and look routine.

rev.note: More analysts are moving EPS estimates up, a quiet support for the bull case.

MSFT.summary: Microsoft’s Azure and AI run-rate remain best-in-class, but capex intensity and cloud-margin dilution are now the key debate.

deposits.note: Monthly deposits cooled from April but LTM inflows remain very strong.

options.note: Options trading intensity is still rising and supports high-margin revenue.

crypto.note: Crypto volume improved sequentially but remains volatile and app crypto is down YoY.

gold.note: Gold subscriber growth keeps building the recurring-revenue leg of the thesis.

arpu.note: ARPU expansion shows better monetization per funded customer.

rs.note: HOOD is sharply outperforming financials today, confirming high-beta momentum.

iv.note: Very rich implied volatility leaves the stock vulnerable to sentiment reversals.

HOOD.summary: Robinhood still has exceptional retail engagement and asset momentum, with crypto cyclicality and rich volatility the main risks.

gm.note: Gross margin is still falling, delaying the core recovery thesis.

inv.note: Inventory remains elevated enough to keep promotional pressure in focus.

markdown.note: Higher discounts are still weighing on ASP and margins across key channels.

china.note: Greater China remains a clear drag and caps any durable re-rating.

dtc.note: Direct and digital softness shows the channel reset is still painful.

rs.note: Nike outperformed XLY today, but one session is not enough to validate a turn.

insider.note: CEO and director purchases are a credible contrarian confidence signal.

NKE.summary: Nike’s turnaround still lacks proof: margins, China and digital remain weak, though insider buying is a modest contrarian positive.

backlog.note: Backlog growth gives unusually strong multi-year visibility.

turbine.note: Gas turbine backlog and slot reservations continue to tighten supply.

gw.note: Contracted GW scale directly supports the power-demand bull case.

dcpower.note: Q1 data-center electrification orders exceeded all of last year.

fcf.note: Q1 free cash flow was exceptional, though quarterly working-capital timing matters.

grid.note: Electrification backlog is large and supports the grid bottleneck thesis.

rs.note: GEV is strongly outperforming industrials, confirming leadership in the tape.

iv.note: Options are moderately rich, with put activity showing some hedging after the run.

insider.note: Insider selling is notable but not large enough to offset operating momentum.

rev.note: Analyst estimate breadth is positive after the Q1 beat and raised guide.

GEV.summary: GE Vernova remains one of the cleanest AI-power beneficiaries, with backlog, GW coverage and FCF all supporting the bull case.
